LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 4.1.1 LISTENING COMPREHENSION: SELECTIVE LISTENING

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 4
Topic 4.1: Listening and Speaking 4.1.1 Listening Comprehension: Selective Listening
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 4.1.1 Listening Comprehension: Selective Listening, part of Strand 4 in Grade 7 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: What can you do to ensure you capture relevant information from a speaker?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. distinguish between specific and general information from a listening text,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 4.1.1 Listening Comprehension: Selective Listening in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. select specific information from a listening text,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 4.1.1 Listening Comprehension: Selective Listening in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. listen and respond to texts on leadership,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 4.1.1 Listening Comprehension: Selective Listening in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. emphasise the value of listening skills in communication.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 4.1.1 Listening Comprehension: Selective Listening in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. distinguish between specific and general information from a listening text,

   Listening and Speaking 4.1.1 Listening Comprehension: Selective Listening helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. select specific information from a listening text,

   Listening and Speaking 4.1.1 Listening Comprehension: Selective Listening helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. listen and respond to texts on leadership,

   Listening and Speaking 4.1.1 Listening Comprehension: Selective Listening helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. emphasise the value of listening skills in communication.

   Listening and Speaking 4.1.1 Listening Comprehension: Selective Listening helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. listen to an audio text and decide whether the information presented is specific or general,

2. search online for audio recordings on leadership and attentively listen to texts for specific information,

3. watch a role play and respond to questions,

4. listen to a passage on leadership (good governance) and answer questions posed by the speaker.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. listen to an audio text and decide whether the information presented is specific or general,
2. search online for audio recordings on leadership and attentively listen to texts for specific information,
3. watch a role play and respond to questions,
4. listen to a passage on leadership (good governance) and answer questions posed by the speaker.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 4.1.1 Listening Comprehension: Selective Listening together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Critical Thinking is developed as the learner listens and selects general and specific information from oral texts.

Values:
• Integrity: It is promoted as the learner nurtures discipline while listening to texts on good governance.

• Social justice: It is enhanced as the learner learns the need for fairness while listening to oral texts on leadership.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

• Good governance is enhanced as the learner listens to texts on leadership.

• Effective communication is achieved as the learner listens and responds to audio texts on good governance.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner relates selective listening to their learning in Kiswahili.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. distinguish between specific and general information from a listening text,
2. select specific information from a listening text,
3. listen and respond to texts on leadership,
4. emphasise the value of listening skills in communication.

Remember the key question: What can you do to ensure you capture relevant information from a speaker?
